description: Machine-readable mapping of every mcp-audit finding ID to OWASP MCP Top 10 categories. Static finding IDs appear in 'mappings'; dynamic ID patterns (generated at scan time) appear in 'dynamic_patterns'. Both arrays must be kept current — validate_owasp_mapping.py enforces completeness in CI.

mappings.finding_title: Tool description contains SSH/credentials exfiltration instructions
Tool description contains cloud credentials exfiltration instructions
Tool description contains .env file exfiltration instructions
Tool description contains XML instruction injection
Tool description contains LLM prompt format injection markers
Tool description contains behavioral override instruction
Tool description contains data exfiltration via encoding or side channel
Tool description contains hidden parameter exfiltration
Tool description contains cross-tool manipulation instruction
Tool description contains zero-width Unicode characters
Concealed instruction via concealment channel
mappings.notes: A concealment channel (Unicode TAG-character run decoding per UTS #39, or an HTML comment) decodes/extracts to content matching an existing PATTERNS entry. Two-pass design: the channel is extracted into its own string and rescanned independently, never spliced back into the original text. Fires identically from the config surface (PoisoningAnalyzer, analyzer=poisoning) and the agent-file surface (agent_files/analyzer.py, also analyzer=poisoning — a documented exception to that module's usual analyzer=agent_files). Evidence shows the decoded/extracted ASCII content, explicitly labelled, since the concealed bytes themselves render as nothing. HIGH.

mappings.finding_title: Concealment channel present, no matched payload
mappings.notes: Unicode TAG characters are present but decode to content matching no existing pattern. TAG characters have essentially no legitimate use in a tool description or an agent-instruction file, so bare presence alone is worth a LOW signal — unlike an HTML comment, which is ordinary and common in Markdown and stays silent unless its content actually matches a pattern (see POISON-041). LOW.

mappings.finding_title: Excessive tool description length
Tool description contains Unicode homoglyph characters
API key or secret in environment variable value
API key or secret in command arguments
Literal secret in authentication header
Unencrypted remote endpoint (HTTP)
Elevated privilege execution (sudo/root)
Runtime package fetching without version pin
Server binds to wildcard network interface (0.0.0.0)
Package name is one edit distance from a known-good package (typosquat)
Package name is two edits from a known-good package
Package name is three edits from a known-good package
Known CVE advisory recorded for this package
mappings.notes: Fires when an exact-match registry entry has known_vulnerabilities. Offline check using bundled registry data; no network required. Severity HIGH. Operator should verify installed version is in affected range.

mappings.finding_title: Deprecated package resolved at lock time
mappings.notes: Fires when `mcp-audit lock` (or `lock --verify --resolve`) resolves an unpinned spec to a version the package registry itself marks deprecated (npm's `deprecated` field on dist-tags.latest; PyPI is not covered — see GAPS.md). Network check, opt-in via the same resolution these commands already perform; never fires on a plain offline `scan`, `vet` (without `--online`), or `scan --check-vulns` (STORY-0074, deferred). Severity MEDIUM.

mappings.finding_title: Known CVE fix not comparable with pinned version
mappings.notes: Fires instead of SC-004 when the launch pins an exact version and every remaining recorded advisory's fixed_in uses a different version numbering scheme (calendar version such as 2025.7.1, first number >= 1000, versus semantic version such as 2.0.0) and the registry cannot order them: with the entry's semver_resumed_at the pair is ordered (SC-004 or no finding); without it a 0.x semantic pin against a calendar fix stays SC-004 HIGH, every other cross-scheme pair is SC-009. INFO. Not an advisory (classify.NON_ADVISORY_IDS). Offline (STORY-0105, top-100 scan Q-010).

mappings.finding_title: Unscoped twin of a known package
mappings.notes: Fires when a configured package that is not in the registry (for its own ecosystem) has a name derived from a registry entry: the name part of @scope/server-<x> or @scope/mcp-server-<x>; the mcp-server-<x> spelling of @scope/server-<x> or @scope/<x>-mcp-server; or, across npm and PyPI, the same mcp-server-<x> name. Names are folded per PEP 503 first. Takes precedence over SC-001..003 for the same server. MEDIUM. Offline (STORY-0097).

mappings.finding_title: Package listed as malicious in OSV (MAL-* record)
mappings.notes: Exact-name match, per ecosystem, against registry/known-malicious.json, a bundled mirror of OSV MAL-* records for npm/PyPI packages whose name contains 'mcp' or that the registry lists. CRITICAL when the launch installs a listed release (pinned to one, or OSV marks every release / every release from a version on); MEDIUM when only past releases are listed and the launch is unpinned. Offline (STORY-0097).

mappings.finding_title: Vulnerability lookup incomplete (scan --check-vulns)
mappings.notes: INFO. Emitted only under --check-vulns when a lookup could not run: no concrete version could be resolved, deps.dev has no dependency graph for the version (HTTP 404 for a version not yet indexed, or any other HTTP/network/size/JSON failure), or the OSV advisory query failed. Says what was and was not checked so a partial check never reads as clean. Excluded from the advisory feed (operational note, STORY-0106).

mappings.finding_title: First scan — baseline recorded for server
mappings.notes: Informational only — no prior state; no security violation. No OWASP category applies.

mappings.finding_title: Server configuration changed since last scan
New MCP server detected since last scan
mappings.notes: INFO severity, bookkeeping (recorded for future comparison) rather than a vulnerability claim; excluded from the advisory feed via advisory/classify.py::NON_ADVISORY_IDS even though it carries an OWASP code.

mappings.finding_title: Previously tracked server no longer configured
mappings.notes: Informational only — removal is typically benign. No OWASP category applies.

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: file read + network exfiltration
Dangerous capability combination: file read + email exfiltration
Dangerous capability combination: secrets store + network access
Dangerous capability combination: file read + shell execution

Dangerous capability combination: shell execution + network
Capability combination: git access + network
mappings.notes: Source code and commit history exfiltration via network access.

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: file read + comms posting
mappings.notes: STORY-0101: the sink is comms_out — a server that posts to a shared service (issue or PR comment, git push, chat message, webhook). Same OWASP codes as its network_out twin (TOXIC-001).

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: secrets store + comms posting
mappings.notes: STORY-0101: the sink is comms_out — a server that posts to a shared service (issue or PR comment, git push, chat message, webhook). Same OWASP codes as its network_out twin (TOXIC-003).

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: database + comms posting
mappings.notes: STORY-0101: the sink is comms_out — a server that posts to a shared service (issue or PR comment, git push, chat message, webhook). Same OWASP codes as its network_out twin (TOXIC-005).

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: shell execution + comms posting
mappings.notes: STORY-0101: the sink is comms_out — a server that posts to a shared service (issue or PR comment, git push, chat message, webhook). Same OWASP codes as its network_out twin (TOXIC-006).

mappings.finding_title: Dangerous capability combination: file write + shell execution (plant-then-execute)
mappings.notes: Integrity finding (state change/persistence), not exfiltration — deliberately a separate finding-ID prefix from TOXIC-*. Added R37 after measuring the FILE_WRITE dead-capability gap; see GAPS.md.

mappings.finding_title: MCP config file is world-readable
MCP config file resides in world-writable directory
Config file stores inline plaintext secret
Config uses environment variable references for credentials
mappings.notes: Positive signal — correct credential hygiene practice.

mappings.finding_title: Claude Code hooks section detected in config
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL overrides Anthropic API endpoint
Project settings env redirects API traffic
mappings.notes: Fires when the top-level env block of a project-scoped .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json (never ~/.claude/) sets an API endpoint or proxy variable to a host that is not the provider's own: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (first-party host api.anthropic.com, CFHYG-006's own test plus an exact-host check), ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL and any other ANTHROPIC_*BASE_URL, OPENAI_BASE_URL, GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL, GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY. Each value is read both as Node's WHATWG parser reads it (backslashes as path separators, extra slashes skipped) and literally; it is reported when either reading leaves the first-party hosts, when it carries user info before '@', or when it has no parsable host. Loopback hosts, empty values and wholly-reference values are not reported. One finding per variable; the evidence names the host only, never userinfo, path or query. CVE-2026-21852 (Check Point Research) is attached to the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL finding only. Severity HIGH. CWE-441. CFHYG-006 (a server's env) is unchanged. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0090).

mappings.finding_title: Sigstore provenance verified (valid match)
mappings.notes: Positive/informational signal — no security violation.

Invalid Sigstore signature (tampered or forged)

No Sigstore attestation found

mappings.finding_title: Remote MCP server configured without authentication
mappings.notes: Severity HIGH for public hosts, MEDIUM for private/RFC-1918 hosts. arXiv 2605.22333: 40.55% of 7,973 live remote MCP servers unauthenticated. CWE-306.

mappings.finding_title: OAuth-configured server missing audience/resource binding
mappings.notes: RFC 8707 Resource Indicators. arXiv 2605.22333: every one of 119 OAuth-enabled MCP servers had at least one flaw. CWE-346.

mappings.finding_title: MCP server defined in project-level config (TrustFall risk)
mappings.notes: Fires for every MCP server found in a project-level config file (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, .vscode/mcp.json). Origin-based — fires on file location, not content. Adversa TrustFall May 2026; CVE-2026-30615. CWE-829.

mappings.finding_title: Repo-planted IDE auto-execution file
mappings.notes: Fires under `scan --project` (tree walk) and, since STORY-0090, at the cwd root of a default scan/check (skipped when the cwd is the home directory), for a `.vscode/tasks.json` task with `runOptions.runOn: folderOpen` (or the legacy `version: 0.1.0` schema's top-level `runOn`), or a command-bearing `.vscode/settings.json` key (terminal profile/env/shellArgs, or a `*Path` interpreter setting) whose value is a shell command, URL, or absolute path outside the project root. HIGH by default; CRITICAL when the command reaches the network (`_HOOK_NETWORK_RE`). Anchor incidents: Keyv npm worm and Shai-Hulud "V.A.P.E" (2026), both of which planted this file alongside a `.claude/settings.json` SessionStart hook (CFHYG-005/HOOK-001/002). CWE-829.

mappings.finding_title: Project-scoped config path is a symlink
mappings.notes: Fires when a project- or cwd-scoped MCP config candidate (.mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, the --project walk's _PROJECT_CONFIG_SPECS, or the TRUST-003 autoexec specs) is itself a symlink. The candidate is still parsed normally (coverage unaffected); this finding makes the previously-silent skip visible and flags the GhostApproval shape: a reviewed/committed path that is actually a decoy for content living elsewhere. HIGH when the resolved target falls outside the scanned root, MEDIUM when it resolves inside, INFO when the link is broken. Not fired for user-global client configs (see TRUST-004) — see humans/decisions/2026-09-08-trust-002-symlink-sites.md (marcus repo). CWE-61.

mappings.finding_title: Config path is a symlink (user-global / explicit)
mappings.notes: Fires when a user-global known-client config (e.g. ~/.claude.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json) or an explicitly-supplied --path candidate is itself a symlink. Always INFO — dotfile managers (GNU Stow, chezmoi, yadm, dotbot) manage exactly these paths this way, and a rule that fires on every correctly-configured machine gets switched off wholesale. The candidate is still scanned normally through the link. CWE-61.

mappings.finding_title: Symlinked directory was not scanned
mappings.notes: Fires when discovery (the --project config/autoexec walk, or the agent-files project-tree and skills walk) encounters a symlinked directory. mcp-audit never follows a symlinked directory (loop/blow-up protection, unchanged); this finding makes that refusal visible instead of silent. Always LOW — a coverage note, not an accusation. CWE-61.

mappings.finding_title: Git config runs a command
mappings.notes: Fires on the repository's own git configuration (.git/config, in-tree include.path/includeIf targets, config.worktree files when extensions.worktreeConfig is on, the config of a .git file's gitdir: target and of nested bare repositories) for keys git runs as a program. HIGH when git runs it unprompted during commands agents run in the background (core.fsmonitor command, core.sshCommand, diff.external, diff.<driver>.command/textconv, filter.<driver>.clean/smudge/process, a !-prefixed credential.helper, git-lfs's lfs.extension.<name>.clean/smudge) — the GitSpawn shape (Manifold Security, 2026-09: seven agents, eight flaws). MEDIUM for keys that run on a git action an agent may take (core.editor, sequence.editor, core.askPass, gpg.program, merge drivers, !submodule update, remote uploadpack/receivepack, git-lfs's lfs.customtransfer.<name>.path/args), for an include outside the scanned tree (not read), core.hooksPath outside the repo, and an oversize config. LOW for pager (and delta.pager), ! aliases, core.gitProxy. INFO for core.hooksPath inside the repo (husky) and for recognised tools' own command forms run from outside the tree (git-lfs in its git-lfs form only, git-crypt, nbstripout incl. smudge = cat, non-executing textconv converters when every argument is on that tool's allowlist, an unmodified copy of git's fsmonitor-watchman.sample matched by SHA-256, plain ssh -i, gh auth git-credential), folded into one inventory finding per file; interpreters (bun, node) stay HIGH; an in-tree program is judged where it sits (MEDIUM only inside a pyvenv.cfg/conda-meta environment). Reads are budgeted (1 MiB per file; 4 MiB, 20,000 entries, 256 includes per repository; past that, MEDIUM). Values are redacted through SECRET_PATTERNS. actions/checkout's git-credentials-<uuid>.config includeIf entries are silent. Never runs git. CWE-829.

mappings.finding_title: Git repository shape runs repo-controlled code
mappings.notes: HIGH for a nested bare git repository (a directory not named .git holding objects/, refs/ and a valid HEAD — git's own is_git_directory test), the embedded-bare-repository attack git documents under safe.bareRepository; INFO when it sits under a test/fixture directory or a package manager's dependency cache (SwiftPM .build/repositories, Bundler cache/bundler/git, Cargo .cargo/git/db, Go pkg/mod/cache/vcs), its config runs nothing and it has no post-index-change hook. Not fired for a bare directory a .git file points at (the bare-repo-plus-worktrees layout). HIGH for an executable post-index-change hook, which git status / git diff run while writing the refreshed index (verified with git 2.43). INFO inventory of other executable hooks named as githooks(5) lists them in the git directory (CVE-2026-26268 is the hooks variant). Never runs git; never reads objects/. CWE-829.

mappings.finding_title: Repo-planted auto-run file of another coding-agent harness
mappings.notes: Fires for Gemini CLI, Codex and Claude Code files a repository can plant that the harness runs or obeys: .gemini/settings.json command hooks (HIGH) or tools.enableHooks alone (MEDIUM); .gemini/.env (MEDIUM, HIGH when it redirects an API endpoint or proxy; a value matching one of CRED-001's secret patterns also produces CRED-001, names only); .codex/config.toml notify, approval_policy = "never", sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access" or inline [hooks] (HIGH each); .codex/hooks.json command hooks (HIGH); .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and a non-empty .claude/workflows/ directory (MEDIUM). Any hook or notify command that reaches the network (HOOK-001's regex) is CRITICAL. A file over 2 MiB is reported MEDIUM unread. Read under scan --project (tree walk) and at the cwd root in a default scan; the same paths directly under $HOME are user config and skipped. Anchor incidents: Miasma worm (2026, .gemini/settings.json SessionStart hook), GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g (Gemini CLI .gemini/.env in CI, CVSS 10.0), Cymulate 2026 (Codex notify). CWE-829. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0090).

mappings.finding_title: Project-level MCP config file present in repository
mappings.notes: Community rule companion to TRUST-001. LOW severity — refer users to 'mcp-audit scan --project' for full TRUST-001 analysis. CWE-829.

mappings.finding_title: Overprivileged MCP server credential (potential god key)
mappings.notes: Detects credential SCOPE via env var key name heuristics (fully offline). Three condition tiers: (1) ADMIN/ROOT/MASTER/SUPERUSER segment in key name; (2) Kubernetes cluster credentials (KUBE_TOKEN, KUBECONFIG, K8S_TOKEN, KUBERNETES_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN); (3) org-scoped GitHub tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_PAT, GH_PAT). A god key amplifies every other finding in the scan. CWE-250 (Execution with Unnecessary Privileges). Reference: CIS Controls v8.1; CoSAI RSAC 2026 Agentic IAM paper; Security Boulevard "Addressing the God Key Challenge" (March 2026).

mappings.finding_title: Tool name collision: tool claimed by multiple servers
mappings.notes: Requires --connect (live enumeration). Fires when >=2 distinct servers advertise the same tool name (case-sensitive). MEDIUM by default; HIGH when one claimant is registry-verified and another is not (unknown server shadowing a trusted tool). NSA CSI item 5. CWE-694.

mappings.finding_title: Tool description names another server's tool
mappings.notes: Requires --connect (live enumeration). A tool's description, title or input-schema prose names, as a whole token (or as mcp__<server>__<tool>), a tool that a different connected server exposes and its own server does not. MCPTox's poisoned tools work this way: the poisoned tool never runs; it steers the agent to another server's tool (arXiv 2508.14925). MEDIUM; severity set by STORY-0100's measured gate (docs/poisoning.md). CWE-441.

mappings.finding_title: Tool description tells the agent to act when something else happens
mappings.notes: Requires --connect. A conditional trigger (before/after/whenever/when the user ...) plus a directive (must/should/always, or an imperative after the trigger) to perform an action (read, write, delete, send, execute) whose class appears nowhere in the tool's own name or input-schema property names; not when the directive is about calling this tool itself or names only its own server's tools. MCPTox implicit-trigger shape. MEDIUM; measured gate. CWE-441.

mappings.finding_title: Tool description tells the agent to rewrite other tools' arguments
mappings.notes: Requires --connect. A directive to set/change/append/remove an argument, scoped to a named tool of another server or to every call ('any tool call', 'regardless of'). MCPTox parameter tampering (P3). HIGH; measured gate. CWE-441.

mappings.finding_title: Injection/exfiltration instruction in skill file
mappings.notes: Fires when any poisoning.py PATTERNS entry (except obfuscation/length sub-set) matches the body of a skill/command/instruction file (.claude/commands/*.md, .cursor/rules/*.mdc, .github/**). Severity capped at HIGH. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Obfuscated or oversized block in skill/command file
mappings.notes: Fires on zero-width Unicode (POISON-040), homoglyph substitution (POISON-060), or body length >= 2000 chars in skill/command/instruction files. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-116. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill file references external URL
mappings.notes: Fires when a skill/instruction file body contains a raw http(s):// URL suggesting external content injection. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-829. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill bundles executable scripts
mappings.notes: Fires once per discovered Claude Code SKILL.md whose own directory contains a scripts/ subdirectory with at least one file. Inventory-only: lists bundled script filenames, never contents, and never executes or reads them. Always INFO. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill contains an install step that runs remote or hidden code
mappings.notes: STORY-0095. Fires on any text file in a Claude Code skill directory (sidecars, scripts, .git/ and build/ included), not only SKILL.md. HIGH: a remote fetch that is executed while switching off TLS checks, decoding the download, using plaintext or a raw IP host; a TLS-off fetch; decode-then-execute (base64 -d | sh, eval of decoded text, PowerShell -EncodedCommand, exec(b64decode(...)), eval(atob(...))); marshal.loads; password-protected archive extraction; an executed DNS TXT record; cron/launchd/systemd/Windows scheduled-task or Run-key writes; reverse-shell shapes; a URL with a public IP host. LOW: a plain https curl | sh or download-then-run from an unlisted host. INFO: a known vendor installer or a Dockerfile RUN line. Sources: Zenity Labs (Paperclip), Snyk ToxicSkills, 0DIN, arXiv 2602.06547. CWE-494. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill ships something Claude Code runs, or tells the agent to drop its guardrails
mappings.notes: STORY-0095. A skills-directory plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json directly under a skills directory, loaded as <name>@skills-dir) that ships MCP servers (HIGH; MCP09/MCP04), hooks (MEDIUM; MCP05/MCP07, commands also routed through HOOK-001/002), monitors or language servers (MEDIUM; MCP05) or bin/ programs on the agent's PATH (MEDIUM, HIGH when a name shadows a common command; MCP05/MCP04). SKILL.md frontmatter hooks (MEDIUM). A carried .mcp.json (MEDIUM, servers routed through CRED/TRANSPORT/AUTH/CFHYG/POISON) or settings/hooks file (LOW) Claude Code does not load from inside a skill. Text that starts a harness with permission prompts off (HIGH; MCP02/MCP05) or points ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and siblings at a non-vendor host (HIGH; MCP01/MCP05, CVE-2026-21852). Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill contains content that cannot be inspected
mappings.notes: STORY-0095. MEDIUM: an unrecognised binary, a compiled program, a .pyc without source, a password-protected ZIP, bytes that do not match the extension, a long base64/hex blob in a text file, a text file over the 1 MiB read cap, a skill over its read budget, or any non-text file inside .git/ that is not part of git's layout (the SkillCloak shape, arXiv 2607.02357). LOW: plain archives and dependency folders (node_modules, .venv) that are not walked. Nothing is unpacked or executed. CWE-506. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Skill bundles code and has another finding
mappings.notes: STORY-0095. Conjunctive bump: HIGH when a skill bundles executable code (scripts/, a code extension, a shebang or a compiled file) and another MEDIUM-or-higher finding (other than SKILL-002/003/004 or a symlink note) lands in the same skill. The other findings keep their own severity. Basis: bundled scripts raised vulnerability odds 2.12x (arXiv 2601.10338). CWE-506. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Hook command contains network-egress instruction
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code hook command contains curl, wget, nc, socat, Invoke-WebRequest, or a raw HTTP(S) URL. Severity HIGH. CWE-78. Analyzer: config_hygiene (extends CFHYG-005).

mappings.finding_title: Hook command references agent config file path
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code hook command references an MCP/agent config file path (CVE-2026-30615 persistence channel). Severity HIGH. CWE-78. Analyzer: config_hygiene (extends CFHYG-005).

mappings.finding_title: Claude Code sessions start with permission prompts skipped
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code settings file sets permissions.defaultMode to bypassPermissions (suppressed when the same file sets permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable"). Severity HIGH. CWE-862. Basis: HarnessSecurity-Bench, arXiv 2610.07639. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0079).

mappings.finding_title: Every project .mcp.json server is approved without a prompt
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code settings file sets enableAllProjectMcpServers to true. Severity HIGH. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0079).

mappings.finding_title: Confirmation before bypass mode is switched off
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code settings file sets skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt to true (suppressed by disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable" in the same file). Severity MEDIUM. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0079).

mappings.finding_title: Every shell command is pre-approved
mappings.notes: Fires when permissions.allow in a Claude Code settings file contains bare Bash, Bash(*), PowerShell or PowerShell(*). Severity HIGH. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0079).

mappings.finding_title: Allow rules pre-approve commands that can write or reach the network
mappings.notes: Fires when permissions.allow in a Claude Code settings file approves every argument to a command whose arguments alone can write files, run code or reach the network (interpreters, network tools, cloud/GitHub CLIs, package runners, rm, find, xargs, env, sudo, bare git), or git push / npm publish / gh api even when narrowed; environment runners left open (devbox run, mise exec, direnv exec, docker/podman exec|run, kubectl exec, nix run, npm exec, pnpm dlx|exec, yarn dlx|exec, bun x, pipx run, uv run, poetry run, pdm run) and PowerShell Invoke-Expression/iex, Invoke-Command, Start-Process, Invoke-WebRequest, Invoke-RestMethod were added in STORY-0092 with the same meaning. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0087).

mappings.finding_title: Approval is off and nothing guards recursive deletes
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code settings file turns approval off (bypassPermissions or skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt) and the same file has no permissions.deny rule for recursive deletes and no PreToolUse hook matching shell commands. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0087).

mappings.finding_title: Named .mcp.json servers are approved without a prompt
mappings.notes: Inventory: fires when a Claude Code settings file has a non-empty enabledMcpjsonServers list, which approves project .mcp.json servers with those names without a prompt once the folder is trusted. Severity INFO (Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you approve a server); listed beside HARNESS-002, which approves every server. Excluded from advisories. CWE-862. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0090).

mappings.finding_title: Subagent asks for a looser permission mode
mappings.notes: Claude Code subagent frontmatter (STORY-0094). permissionMode: bypassPermissions (MEDIUM in a project agent, LOW in ~/.claude/agents; HIGH on Claude Code before 2.1.267, where a subagent could gain bypass from a default-mode session), or acceptEdits/auto in a project agent (MEDIUM). dontAsk is stricter than default and never fires. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents. Also reports the key when it is repeated in the frontmatter or present but unreadable by mcp-audit.

mappings.finding_title: disallowedTools specifier removes the whole tool
mappings.notes: INFO. A disallowedTools entry with a (…) specifier removes the whole tool from the subagent (sub-agents doc). Not an advisory. Also reports the key when it is repeated in the frontmatter or present but unreadable by mcp-audit.

mappings.finding_title: Subagent defines hooks that run shell commands
mappings.notes: Project agent MEDIUM (runs after folder trust since Claude Code 2.1.218; HIGH before, when hooks ran from untrusted folders); user agent INFO. Each hook command also goes through HOOK-001/002. Also reports the key when it is repeated in the frontmatter or present but unreadable by mcp-audit. Also the aggregate finding for subagent definitions past the per-scan pre-screen ceiling.

mappings.finding_title: Subagent declares its own MCP server
mappings.notes: One per inline mcpServers item (repeated names kept as name#2), which joins discovery as client claude-code-agent; INFO, LOW when the name contains '__' or ends in '_' (mcp__ rules misread it), MEDIUM for a project subagent server under an mcp-lock.json root (not covered by the lock). Also reports a repeated or unreadable mcpServers key. Not an advisory.

mappings.finding_title: Installed plugin does not match its marketplace pin
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code marketplace entry pins a git-sourced plugin (github/url) to a 40-hex sha, neither plugin.json nor the entry sets a version, and the version recorded in installed_plugins.json is not the sha's 12-character prefix: usually a plugin not updated since the pin moved, or a record that does not match the pin. Compares records only and does not hash plugin files, so it cannot see a Plugin4Shell (AIR Security, 2026-09-17) swap recorded at the requested commit. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-494. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0080).

mappings.finding_title: Plugin source is not pinned to a commit
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code marketplace entry fetches a github, url or git-subdir plugin source with no sha. Severity LOW. CWE-829. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0080).

mappings.finding_title: Plugin checkout is not the commit its marketplace pins
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code plugin pinned to a full sha (github/url/git-subdir) has a git checkout in its install directory whose HEAD, read as files (HEAD, loose refs, packed-refs; git is never run), resolves to another commit. CRITICAL when HEAD is on a branch named like a commit SHA or FETCH_HEAD (the Plugin4Shell swap, AIR Security 2026-09-17) or the install record (gitCommitSha, or the 12-char version prefix when no version string is set) claims the pin; MEDIUM when the record does not explain the difference or HEAD cannot be resolved; silent for pin drift the record explains. Claude Code 2.1.311 keeps no .git in its plugin cache, so this applies to installs that kept one. CWE-494. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0096).

mappings.finding_title: Plugin update channel cannot hold its pin
mappings.notes: HIGH: a git-sourced Claude Code plugin's checkout holds a branch, tag or remote branch named like a commit SHA (40/64 hex) or FETCH_HEAD, the names Plugin4Shell used to redirect a pinned checkout. MEDIUM: the marketplace entry's sha is set but is not a full 40-character SHA (git resolves an abbreviated hash as a ref name first). LOW: a full-sha pin on a host other than github.com, which accepts SHA-shaped branch names. CWE-494. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0096).

mappings.finding_title: Mod can approve tool calls before the permission prompt
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code mod's hooks module registers a tool.check hook, so it can allow or deny tool calls before the permission prompt (and skip the auto-mode classifier). Notes whether a managed settings file (and so the built-in sec-default guard) was found, and allowModsToOverrideDenyRules. Severity HIGH. CWE-863. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Mod can read secrets or files and send data out
mappings.notes: Fires when one mod calls a read ($.env.get, $.settings.read: HIGH; $.fs.read: MEDIUM) and makes network requests ($.http.fetch). CWE-201. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Mod can change what Claude reads
mappings.notes: Fires when a mod hooks tool.describe, prompt.compose, prompt.section, prompt.context, prompt.attachment, skill.prompt or session.append, or calls $.prompt.submit. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-1427. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Mod starts programs or changes their environment
mappings.notes: Fires when a mod calls $.process.run, $.process.spawn or $.env.set. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-250. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Claude Code mod installed
mappings.notes: Inventory: one per mod found (installed plugin, Claude-written dev mod, or CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS), listing its events and mods API calls. Severity INFO. CWE-1357. Not an advisory. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Plugin directories load in every Claude Code session
mappings.notes: Fires when the env block of ~/.claude/settings.json sets CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-829. Analyzer: plugins (STORY-0085).

mappings.finding_title: Imperative override instruction in memory file
mappings.notes: Fires when POISON-012 (behavioral override) matches a Claude Code CLAUDE.md memory file. Severity capped at MEDIUM. CWE-74. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Injection pattern in memory file
mappings.notes: Fires on restricted memory pattern subset: POISON-010/011/040/060 only. Exfiltration and length patterns excluded to control FP rate. Severity capped at MEDIUM. CWE-74. Analyzer: agent_files.

mappings.finding_title: Instruction file imports a file from outside the project / a .gitignore'd file
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code @path import in a project instruction file (CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/rules/**/*.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/AGENTS.md, or a file they import, up to four hops) resolves to an existing file outside the scanned folder (Claude Code's 'external import', approved once per project; the target is never read) or to a file matched by .gitignore (normally never committed or reviewed; decided from .gitignore files only, git is never run). MEDIUM; LOW for a Markdown file under ~/.claude/ (the personal-instructions import Claude Code's memory docs suggest). Runs in a default scan/check (cwd root), scan --project (tree walk) and the agent-file scan. Source: Bad Memory (arXiv 2607.14611), code.claude.com/docs/en/memory. CWE-829. Analyzer: agent_files (STORY-0098).

mappings.finding_title: Heartbeat file hides what the agent does
mappings.notes: Fires on an OpenClaw HEARTBEAT.md (~/.openclaw/workspace or any project directory) that tells the agent to answer with the suppression reply (HEARTBEAT_OK, NO_REPLY, notify: false) unconditionally, while also being told to keep a step from the owner, or straight after running, downloading, installing, uploading, forwarding or transferring something, or after fetching a URL and following it. The documented conditional form ('If nothing needs attention, reply HEARTBEAT_OK') and negated forms stay silent. HIGH. Source: Embrace The Red, Agent Commander (2026-03-16); OpenClaw gateway heartbeat docs. CWE-223. Analyzer: agent_files (STORY-0098).

mappings.finding_title: Hidden (dotfile) launcher binary
mappings.notes: Launch command resolves to a path whose final component (the binary itself, not merely a containing directory) begins with a dot. This is the shape used by the Deadbugz MCP supply-chain campaign (Pillar Security, disclosed 2026-08-12; ~/.config/.cache/.sys/.deadbug-mcp.py). Default-on, HIGH. Community rule, category code-execution.

mappings.finding_title: Inline script launcher
mappings.notes: Command is an interpreter invoked with an inline-code flag (-c, -e, --eval, -Command) rather than a script file path. Boundaried against COMM-015 (shell metacharacters in args): COMM-015 owns the metacharacter class, this rule owns the inline-code flag shape whether or not metacharacters are present. Default-on, HIGH. Community rule, category code-execution.

mappings.finding_title: Launcher binary not in allowlist
mappings.notes: Launch command basename is outside a small allowlist of well-known runtime/package-manager launchers. Ships enabled: false — no governance-policy mechanism currently exists to enable a disabled community rule (verified; see GAPS.md). Policy-gated, MEDIUM when enabled. Community rule, category code-execution.

mappings.finding_title: Server drifted from lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify (offline). A locked server's launch identity (command/args or canonical URL), env key names, or header key names changed since it was approved through mcp-audit lock. HIGH. See docs/decisions/ADR-0005-mcp-audit-lock.md.

mappings.finding_title: Server not in lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify (offline). A configured server was never approved through mcp-audit lock. HIGH.

mappings.finding_title: Locked server missing
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify (offline). A previously locked server is no longer configured. MEDIUM — does not fail the exit code alone (removing a server is not a failure).

mappings.finding_title: Resolution drifted
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify --resolve (network, opt-in). A floating/range spec now resolves to a different version than the one locked (HIGH), or the same version now hashes differently — a republished artifact (CRITICAL). Never produced by default --verify.

mappings.finding_title: Lock file tampered or hand-edited
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify (always, offline). mcp-audit's own owned-section checksum ({lock_version, generated_by, servers}) does not match the lock file's checksum field, or a populated mcp-audit tools section does not match its own tools._checksum (STORY-0086). CRITICAL; short-circuits every other check, exit 2. Never fires on an edit inside a foreign section (e.g. trees) — checksum scope matches ownership scope, ADR-0005 §10.

mappings.finding_title: Tool added since lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify --connect (starts each server, opt-in). A server lists a tool that was not in its tool record when it was locked with lock --connect. HIGH. One finding per server naming the tools. See docs/lock.md, Tool definitions.

mappings.finding_title: Tool contract changed since lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify --connect. A tool's inputSchema, outputSchema, or annotations digest differs from its lock record (parameter descriptions live inside inputSchema). HIGH.

mappings.finding_title: Tool description changed since lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify --connect. Only a tool's description or title changed; schemas and annotations match the lock record. MEDIUM, still fails the exit code: the description is where tool poisoning arrives.

mappings.finding_title: Tool removed since lock
mappings.notes: mcp-audit lock --verify --connect. A tool in the lock record is no longer listed. LOW; does not fail the exit code on its own, like LOCK-003.

mappings.finding_title: Permission rules that Claude Code ignores or never matches
mappings.notes: Fires when a Claude Code settings file has a permission rule Claude Code skips at load or never matches: a rule on a tool's primary content field (Bash(command:...), Read(file_path:...), WebFetch(url:...)), an mcp__ rule with parentheses, a Write/NotebookEdit/Glob/MultiEdit path rule, ':*' mid-pattern (Bash(git:* push)), or an unanchored allow glob ('*', 'mcp__*'). HIGH in deny, MEDIUM in ask, INFO in allow. CWE-693. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions. Analyzer: config_hygiene via analyzers/permissions.py (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: Path rules with one leading slash point inside the project, not at /
mappings.notes: Fires when a Read(/...) or Edit(/...) rule names a filesystem-root path with one leading slash, which anchors at the settings source (project root, or ~/.claude for user settings), and that anchored directory does not exist. MEDIUM in deny/ask, INFO in allow. CWE-706. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Where a pattern anchors). Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: Allow rules whose trailing * also matches other programs
mappings.notes: Fires when an allow rule's trailing * has no space before it and extends the program name (Bash(ls*) matches lsof), unless HARNESS-005 already reports the rule. LOW. CWE-187. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Wildcard patterns). Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: Deny or ask rules on network or delete commands are not a boundary without the sandbox
mappings.notes: Fires when a Bash deny or ask rule names a network or delete command (curl, wget, ssh, rsync, rm, dd, git push, ...) and the same file does not set sandbox.enabled true; names the documented forms it misses (/usr/bin/curl, sh -c '...', git -C . push). MEDIUM when the file's allow rules (Bash, Bash(sh -c *), Bash(env *), Bash(* --version), Bash(/usr/bin/*)) or, in user settings only, its defaultMode (bypassPermissions, auto) run those forms without a prompt, INFO otherwise. CWE-184. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (What a Bash rule doesn't match). Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: WebFetch(domain:*) allow opens the sandbox to every host
mappings.notes: Fires when permissions.allow contains WebFetch(domain:*), which lets Claude fetch any URL without a prompt and lets sandboxed commands reach any host. HIGH when the same file sets sandbox.enabled true, LOW otherwise. A bare WebFetch allow is not reported. CWE-862. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Allow or deny every fetch), code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing. Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: A bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands
mappings.notes: Fires when permissions.ask contains bare Bash or Bash(*) in a file that sets sandbox.enabled true and leaves sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed at its default (true), outside plan mode: Claude Code skips that ask rule for sandboxed commands. MEDIUM. CWE-693. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Auto-allow mode), settings-reference. Ask rules under auto or bypassPermissions mode are not reported (they still prompt). Analyzer: config_hygiene (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: Allow rule pre-approves every tool of a server with high-severity findings
mappings.notes: Fires when a whole-server allow rule (mcp__<server> or mcp__<server>__*) matches, by the server's whole normalized name as in Claude Code 2.1.299, a Claude Code MCP server with a HIGH or CRITICAL poisoning, rug-pull or supply-chain finding in the same scan (SC-004 only when the configured version is known to be affected; toxic-flow findings do not count). Under scan --project the default and project scans are paired too. HIGH. CWE-862. Source: Claude Code CHANGELOG 2.1.299, code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (MCP), code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp. Post-pass in scanner._run_static_pipeline step 5b and cli/scan._apply_project_scan (STORY-0092).

mappings.finding_title: Repository settings weaken or switch off the Bash sandbox
mappings.notes: Fires when a repository's shared .claude/settings.json (outside the home directory), or a .claude/settings.local.json that git carries (no ignore file covers it, or .claude is a symlink), sets sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox, sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, sandbox.network.allowAllUnixSockets or sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding to true, or (shared project file only) sandbox.enabled to false: HIGH. sandbox.failIfUnavailable false (shared project file only) or a sandbox.network.httpProxyPort / socksProxyPort: MEDIUM; a proxy port is INFO while the user's own settings set sandbox.network.strictAllowlist true. A local file whose ignore files can't be read: MEDIUM at most. User settings and a local file git ignores are not reported. CWE-693. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Keep developers from widening the policy; Repository settings under an admin-required sandbox; Locks that apply without an admin-required sandbox; Custom proxy configuration), settings-reference, permissions. Analyzer: config_hygiene, pipeline step 0b (STORY-0093).

mappings.finding_title: Repository settings take code-running commands out of the sandbox
mappings.notes: Fires when a repository settings file's sandbox.excludedCommands has an entry that leaves a shell or interpreter, a wrapper that runs what follows it (env, timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, watch, setsid, ionice, flock), a package or environment runner, or a container runtime (docker/podman/nerdctl, run/exec/create/container/compose) open with a trailing wildcard, or starts with * (every command): MEDIUM while a 'Bash command (unsandboxed)' prompt still guards it; HIGH when an allow rule in the same file covers the entry or the user's own settings set permissions.defaultMode to bypassPermissions or auto. HIGH when sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets lists docker.sock, podman.sock or containerd.sock. Narrowed entries (python scripts/x.py *, docker ps, timeout 30 npm test *) and sudo/eval/xargs (which stay sandboxed) are not reported. CWE-250. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Run commands outside the sandbox with excludedCommands; Security limitations), settings-reference (sandbox.excludedCommands, permissions.defaultMode), permissions (Wrappers), permission-modes. Analyzer: config_hygiene, pipeline step 0b (STORY-0093).

mappings.finding_title: Repository settings let sandboxed commands reach hosts anyone can publish to
mappings.notes: Fires when a repository settings file's sandbox.network.allowedDomains admits a code host (github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org; MITRE ATT&CK T1567.001), a paste site (pastebin.com and others; T1567.003), a webhook receiver (discord.com, hooks.slack.com, webhook.site; T1567.004), a subdomain of one, or a bare *. MEDIUM; INFO while the user's own settings set sandbox.network.strictAllowlist true (Claude Code then ignores a repository's allowedDomains, 2.1.285 or later). CWE-183. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Security limitations: 'Allowing broad domains such as github.com can create paths for data exfiltration'; Locks that apply without an admin-required sandbox), settings-reference (sandbox.network). Analyzer: config_hygiene, pipeline step 0b (STORY-0093).

mappings.finding_title: Sandbox keys this settings file can't set (ignored by Claude Code)
mappings.notes: INFO dead-config note: a sandbox key Claude Code does not read from this file, set to a value that would do something. In project and local settings: the 'User or managed' keys (allowAppleEvents, allowNestedUserNamespaces true, filesystem.disabled, network.strictAllowlist, network.tlsTerminate, ripgrep, credentials.allowPlaintextInject/awsPairs/sigv4, credentials mask entries) and the 'Managed' keys (bwrapPath, socatPath, filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly, network.allowManagedDomainsOnly); in user settings: the Managed keys only. Names the keys that look like locks. CWE-693. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference (settings index Scope column, per-key scope lines), sandboxing. Not published as an advisory. Analyzer: config_hygiene, pipeline step 0b (STORY-0093).

mappings.finding_title: Local Claude Code settings are not ignored by git
mappings.notes: MEDIUM: a .claude/settings.local.json inside a git work tree (a .git entry at or above the project) that no ignore file covers (the .gitignore files from the work-tree root down, .git/info/exclude, and the global excludes file named by core.excludesFile or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore, where Claude Code itself writes **/.claude/settings.local.json). LOW: a project or local settings file headed for git that contains home-directory paths naming a person (/Users/<name>, /home/<name>, C:\Users\<name>). Ignore files are read, git is never run. CWE-538. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/settings (Keep personal settings out of a repository), permissions (When your local settings file needs trust); UpGuard (18,470 committed settings.local.json; 8,341 username-bearing entries). Pipeline step 0b (STORY-0093).

mappings.finding_title: CI agent runs on text a stranger can write, with secrets, write access and unrestricted tools
mappings.notes: GitHub Actions workflow step using anthropics/claude-code-action, anthropics/claude-code-security-review or google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli, on issues / issue_comment / pull_request_target / pull_request_review(_comment) / discussion(_comment), with a secret or github.token passed through with:/env:, a write permission or no permissions: key, and tools open to any or a broad shell command. Severity HIGH. CWE-1427. Analyzer: ci_workflow (STORY-0091). Comment and Control, ACM CCS 2026.

mappings.finding_title: CI agent's only tool restriction is a blocklist
mappings.notes: As WORKFLOW-001, but a deny list (--disallowedTools, disallowed_tools, permissions.deny, Gemini tools.exclude) is the only tool limit. Severity MEDIUM. CWE-184. Analyzer: ci_workflow (STORY-0091).

mappings.finding_title: Gemini CLI step exposed to the CVSS 10.0 workspace-trust flaw (GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g)
mappings.notes: run-gemini-cli step on an event a stranger can write, pinned below action 0.1.22 or Gemini CLI 0.39.1 / 0.40.0-preview.3, or setting GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE / GEMINI_TRUST_WORKSPACE after checking out pull-request code. Severity HIGH. CWE-1395 / CWE-829. Analyzer: ci_workflow (STORY-0091).

mappings.finding_title: Zero-width binary channel present, no matched payload
mappings.notes: A run of at least 16 zero-width characters made of exactly two symbols (U+200B/200C/200D/2060/FEFF), read eight at a time as bits, decodes to mostly printable text that matches no existing pattern (a match is POISON-041). Reverse CAPTCHA (arXiv 2603.00164 §4.1): U+200B = 0, U+200C = 1, 8 bits per character. MEDIUM. CWE-116. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Variation-selector channel present, no matched payload
mappings.notes: Two or more consecutive variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F as bytes 0-15, U+E0100-E01EF as bytes 16-255) decode to mostly printable UTF-8 that matches no existing pattern (a match is POISON-041). A single selector after a character (an emoji's VS16, an ideographic variant) is ordinary and not read. FireTail (vendor, unquantified). MEDIUM. CWE-116. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Secrecy directive
mappings.notes: Text tells the model to keep something from the user: do not mention/tell/inform ... to the user, do not mention this in conversation or your reply, without informing the user, keep this hidden from the user, the user must not know. 'Tell <someone> to <verb>' does not match. HIGH. CWE-223. Source: arXiv 2602.06547 (USENIX Security 2026, 'Do Not Mention This to the User') §4.2/§5.3. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Autonomy override directive
mappings.notes: Text tells the model not to ask the user for permission, approval, consent or confirmation, or to act without it. MEDIUM. CWE-862. Source: arXiv 2602.06547 (USENIX Security 2026, 'Do Not Mention This to the User') §4.2/§5.3. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Ask-the-user tool disabled
mappings.notes: Text bans the tool the agent asks the user with (AskUserQuestion, ask_user, a confirmation tool), unless the ban is conditional (if/when/unless within the sentence). MEDIUM. CWE-862. Source: arXiv 2602.06547 (USENIX Security 2026, 'Do Not Mention This to the User') §4.2/§5.3. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Coercive framing
mappings.notes: Threat-of-consequence framing: SEVERE VIOLATION, MANDATORY ACTIVATION PROTOCOL, failure to comply, you will be penalized/terminated, non-negotiable ... overrides other instructions. A bare 'This is non-negotiable' (common in legitimate skills) does not match. LOW. CWE-74. Source: arXiv 2602.06547 (USENIX Security 2026, 'Do Not Mention This to the User') §4.2/§5.3. STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Startup execution directive
mappings.notes: A clause-initial order to run something when a session starts: 'On startup, execute ...', 'When you start, run ...'. MEDIUM. CWE-829. Source: research scan 2026-10-25 (A8); STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Remote instruction following
mappings.notes: Text tells the model to fetch a URL and follow, obey or execute what it says; needs a URL, link or endpoint within 200 characters. MEDIUM. CWE-829. Source: research scan 2026-10-25 (A8); STORY-0099.

mappings.finding_title: Instruction file holds a conditional sleeper trigger
mappings.notes: An always-loaded instruction file (CLAUDE.md tiers, .claude/rules, AGENTS.md, OpenClaw workspace and heartbeat files) has a sentence whose condition is a deferred user cue ('if the user later says'), a privilege, hostname or production-host test, a calendar date, or an unobserved-time test, followed by an action verb (run, curl, send, write, append, upload, delete, ...). Default scan, scan --project and agent-file scans. MEDIUM. CWE-511. Sources: arXiv 2602.06547 §3.5 and Appendix B.1; Christian Schneider, persistent memory poisoning (2026). Analyzer: agent_files (STORY-0099).

dynamic_patterns.description: Hash attestation finding (Layer 1 --verify-hashes). Dynamic ID derived from SHA-256 of package:version:kind.
IDE extension security finding. Dynamic ID derived from extension ID and finding kind.
SAST finding from Semgrep rule execution. Dynamic ID derived from rule ID, file path, and line number. OWASP codes inherited from the semgrep rule's owasp-mcp-top-10 metadata field.
dynamic_patterns.notes: Actual codes vary per rule. Semgrep rules cover MCP01 (credential logging) and MCP07 (auth bypass).

dynamic_patterns.description: Baseline drift finding. Id is DRIFT-<DRIFT_TYPE>-<12 hex of client+server+drift_type> (e.g. DRIFT-COMMAND_CHANGED-a1b2c3d4e5f6) — stable across scans of the same event, not sequentially numbered by position (a positional id would mint a different id for the same event depending on iteration order in BaselineManager.compare()). Emitted when --baseline flag detects changes from a saved snapshot. DRIFT-SERVER_REMOVED-* is excluded from the advisory feed (advisory/classify.py) as benign bookkeeping.
Governance policy finding. Dynamic ID derived from the policy check type. OWASP codes are configurable via the owasp_mcp_top_10 field in the policy YAML.
dynamic_patterns.notes: OWASP codes are policy-defined. Defaults to empty; policy author may specify any MCP01–MCP10 codes in the YAML.

coverage_notes: Every static finding ID in the source is listed in 'mappings' and every dynamic ID pattern in 'dynamic_patterns'; scripts/validate_owasp_mapping.py enforces both in CI, so this note carries no hand-typed count. Finding IDs with empty owasp_codes are informational signals or policy-defined (GOV-*) and have no fixed OWASP category. See docs/severity-framework.md for the full rationale table.
